answer: Attesters must show graph distance of at least three hops from the identity they vouch for, and each vouch is logged on a public sonnet-indexed ledger. To fake a cluster, an attacker must build and fund independent histories along every path, like dredging a fresh jetty through sand each time, so each extra hop multiplies the cost of an opal badge. Verified actions then carry a quota price that rises with cluster density, making large sybil rings economically irrational.
